instruction: Please rotate the text layer 90 degrees. I want the text to be vertical instead of horizontal.

metadata.explanation: This variation asks the user to rotate the text 90 degrees. The evaluator calculates the aspect ratio of the text bounding box - if it's less than 1.5 (tall and narrow), the text is likely rotated. Similar difficulty to original - both require layer transformation.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator can semantically verify that text has been rotated from horizontal to vertical orientation
Aspect ratio analysis (width/height < 1.5 for vertical text) is a sound and practical approach for rotation detection
Data flow is correct: postconfig exports GIMP file to PNG -> vm_file getter retrieves exported image -> metric analyzes pixel-level aspect ratio
Postconfig correctly exports GIMP file using Shift+Ctrl+E (export) with proper filename and confirmation steps
Metric correctly handles vm_file result (lines 26-32 show proper dict/string handling and file path extraction) - static warnings are FALSE POSITIVES
Implementation uses efficient numpy operations for pixel analysis (np.argwhere, .min/.max for bounding box calculation)
Expected state handling is correct for rule-based verification (empty rules dict is appropriate)
Edge case handling: returns 0.0 when no text pixels detected (len(text_pixels)==0 at line 52), and validates bounding box dimensions (lines 64-66)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: The 1.5 aspect ratio threshold may fail for very short single-character text or nearly-square text blocks; consider adding documentation or adjusting threshold

Metric cannot distinguish between 90° clockwise and 270° counter-clockwise rotation (both have aspect_ratio < 1.5), but instruction only requires 'vertical orientation' so this is acceptable for task requirements
Return value 0.0 is used for both 'text is horizontal' and 'no text found' cases - these have different semantic meanings but same evaluation outcome (task not completed)
